gaps.explanation: Per fund, GAAP fund statement pp6-7 total revenues vs the budget-basis schedule (Actual Amounts) in detail: General Fund 8,143,482 vs p14 11,403,191 (Taxes 6,828,169, Intergovernmental 138,063, Local 4,436,959) = -3,259,709; Streets 3,757,848 vs p15 3,681,695 = +76,153; Economic Development 1,970,588 vs p16 1,917,194 = +53,394; Debt Service 303,447 vs p17 284,840 = +18,607; Special Projects 371,175 vs p18 499,641 = -128,466; Capital Projects 1,027,038 vs p19 1,044,842 = -17,804; Other Governmental Funds 1,544,245 vs combining statement pp20-21 columns 1,544,245 = 0. Net -3,257,825; the JSON statement total 17,117,827 (Total-column rows) vs fund columns 17,117,823 (+4) and detail line rounding (-1) give the listed -3,257,822. Every fund is in detail once; no column, row or page is missing; no subtotal, prior-year or budget column recorded. The budget schedules print no other financing rows, while the General Fund statement column prints Operating transfers in 3,396,423 and Proceeds from sale of assets 31,407 (both in detail as other-financing lines from p6); the report does not print what the GF budget-basis 'Local' 4,436,959 contains, so no line can be shown to be the same money and none is removed. Report-printed basis difference (budgetary vs GAAP).

Net +33,165; JSON statement total 19,102,068 vs fund columns 19,102,067 (+1) gives the listed 33,166. Each budget schedule prints a single function row (e.g. Debt Service 'General government' 245,748 vs GAAP Debt Service capital outlay 499,126); no fund or row is missing and nothing is counted twice. Budgetary vs GAAP basis.
